<reflection>
The second experiment (S=1.0 M, cat=0.05 M) provided additional data, but the total negative log-likelihoods across both runs show that many mechanisms remain closely clustered, with M2 currently the best fit. The aim of probing catalyst concentration dependence was partially achieved, as likelihoods shifted, but significant ambiguity persists among some 14 mechanisms. A new experiment is needed to further discriminate within this large plausible set.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose to vary the substrate concentration to a low value (0.2 M) while keeping catalyst at 0.01 M (as in the first run) and no initial product. This condition will probe the substrate dependence of the initial rate. Mechanisms that involve substrate inhibition (e.g., M11) or multiple substrate binding (e.g., M7) may show deviations from simple first-order behavior at low substrate. Dimerization-related mechanisms (e.g., M2, M3, M13) may also exhibit different effective orders because substrate binding can shift monomer-dimer equilibria. By contrasting with the first run (S=1.0 M, same catalyst), we obtain a clear profile of how rate scales with substrate concentration, which is informative for many mechanisms simultaneously without pushing into saturation or depletion extremes.
</hypothesis>
